Deployment inventory includes blow-verdict, direct instruction, question, spatial reversal, and the compound 'the matter under your heels' (腳跟下事). Family check with heel (腳跟), underfoot (腳下), on the spot (立地), one's own part (本分), thirty blows (三十棒), and atop the head (頭上) supports one spatial referent used in several interview acts. Literal and loaded uses were not split because the loaded deployment keeps the same deictic location rather than naming a different thing.

Senses.Explanation: “Right under your heels” locates what is immediately beneath one’s stance and recurs in demands to inspect, cut off, or pass what lies there. Chan interviews repeatedly turn this ordinary location back upon the person questioned. A reply can be appraised with 'right under your heels, thirty blows would be fitting'; Poshan Haiming can ask 'how deep is the water under your heels?', direct a questioner to 'recognize it right under your heels,' or answer a request for direct pointing with 'look clearly right under your heels.' The phrase also marks relative position in a public comparison: if the unnamed monastic can distinguish the kinds of leakage, Dongshan is under his heels; if not, he is under Dongshan's heels. A stock question asks about 'the matter under your heels' and receives 'putting a head atop your head.' The Chan-specific bend is consistent and observable: the spatial phrase becomes the immediate locus of an interviewer's demand, appraisal, or reversal, often contrasted with what the questioner seeks elsewhere or above. The texts do not supply a further object hidden beneath the feet, and neither does this entry.
